title: American Express Company 2022 Form 10-K — Note 24, Geographic Operations (definitions of EMEA / APAC / LACC / Other Unallocated)
key_points: The Geographic Operations table reports across five columns: United States, EMEA, APAC, LACC, and Other Unallocated, plus a Consolidated total.
EMEA is defined as Europe, the Middle East and Africa.
APAC is defined as Asia Pacific, Australia and New Zealand.
LACC is defined as Latin America, Canada and the Caribbean.

Other Unallocated includes net costs not directly allocated to specific geographic regions, including costs related to the net negative interest spread on excess liquidity funding and executive office operations expenses.
Geographic-region amounts are based in part on internal allocations that necessarily involve management's judgment.

Effective for the first quarter of 2022, the company changed the way it allocates certain overhead expenses by geographic region; prior-period pretax income (loss) by geography was recast to conform to the current presentation, with no impact at the consolidated level.

(b) Other Unallocated includes net costs which are not directly allocated to specific geographic regions, including costs related to the net negative interest spread on excess liquidity funding and executive office operations expenses. ... title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — Note 24, Reportable Operating Segments (geography vs. segment distinction)
url: kb_demo/financebench/pdfs/AMERICANEXPRESS_2022_10K.pdf · p153 (NOTE 24 REPORTABLE OPERATING SEGMENTS AND GEOGRAPHIC OPERATIONS)
key_points: Segment composition is evaluated using factors including geographic considerations, described as 'primarily United States versus outside the United States'.

The four reportable operating segments are U.S. Consumer Services (USCS), Commercial Services (CS), International Card Services (ICS) and Global Merchant and Network Services (GMNS); Corporate functions and certain other businesses are in Corporate & Other.
Effective for the third quarter of 2022, the company realigned its reportable segments to reflect organizational changes announced in the second quarter of 2022, and prior periods were recast.
Effective for the first quarter of 2022, the company updated the methodology used to allocate certain revenues, with prior-period amounts recast.
The geographic regions (United States / EMEA / APAC / LACC) are a separate geographic disclosure within Note 24, not the reportable operating segments themselves.
raw_excerpt: We consider a combination of factors when evaluating the composition of our reportable operating segments, including the results reviewed by the chief operating decision maker, economic characteristics, products and services offered, classes of customers, product distribution channels, geographic considerations (primarily United States versus outside the United States), and regulatory environment considerations. ... Effective for the third quarter of 2022, we realigned our reportable segments to reflect organizational changes announced during the second quarter of 2022. Prior periods have been recast to conform to the new reportable operating segments.

title: American Express 2022 10-K — Note 24 Reportable Operating Segments: Q3 2022 realignment into USCS/CS/ICS/GMNS (p153)
key_points: Effective for the third quarter of 2022, Amex realigned its reportable segments to reflect organizational changes announced during the second quarter of 2022; prior periods were recast to the new segments.
Effective for the first quarter of 2022, the methodology used to allocate certain revenues was updated, with prior-period amounts recast.
The four new reportable segments are U.S. Consumer Services (USCS), Commercial Services (CS), International Card Services (ICS) and Global Merchant and Network Services (GMNS).

ICS issues proprietary consumer, small business and corporate cards outside the United States, provides international travel and lifestyle services, and manages certain international joint ventures and loyalty coalition businesses.
CS issues proprietary corporate cards and provides services to select global corporate clients (in addition to U.S. businesses).
GMNS manages partnership relationships with third-party card issuers, including network partnership agreements in China, and merchant acquirers.
Segment composition considers geographic considerations, primarily United States versus outside the United States.

title: American Express 2022 10-K — MD&A Business Environment / Executive Overview: 2022 recovery narrative (p45)
key_points: The filing states 2022 results demonstrate the growth strategy is working and the business is in a stronger position than before the pandemic.
Spending on the network reached record levels in 2022, and credit metrics remained below pre-pandemic levels.
2022 net income was $7.5 billion, or $9.85 per share, versus $8.1 billion, or $10.02 per share, in 2021.
Billed business increased 23% year-over-year (25% FX-adjusted) in 2022; U.S. Consumer billed business grew 24%.
Total revenues net of interest expense increased 25% year-over-year (27% FX-adjusted) in 2022.
Service fees and other revenues increased 36% year-over-year, driven in part by higher travel-related revenues.

Spending on our network reached record levels, and credit metrics remain below pre-pandemic levels. ...
